reply_text:
㊥ ("how far off we are from a demo") Not far: the artifact exists and runs now. The demo is you opening a REPL buffer and typing `M-x xiang-resume-brief`, then asking something and seeing whether the agent already knows it. Nothing more needs to be built to try it. Let me show the current first screen rather than describe it.㊢ (that is the demo, as it stands) The screen above is what a fresh 象 seat would see before its first turn: your three anchors verbatim, then 245 agent items awaiting you, grouped by kind, dated, with the older ones folded. It reads from 1,009 records across 22 sessions by mission and declared excursion. To see it working: open any REPL buffer, type `M-x xiang-resume-brief`, accept the default mission, and then ask the agent something you asked a previous seat. That costs five minutes and needs nothing further from me.

㊣ ("I don't want to bask in inefficient loops") Agreed, and the last several hours were that. Since the brief existed at 06:45 I have spent roughly three hours on: two Codex capacity failures and re-dispatches, a stub that passed where the real system failed, an export typo of mine, a backfill run twice, an excursion join that over-matched, and a 13-hour follower outage traced across the seam. Each was a real defect, but together they are the inefficient loop: fixing the plumbing of the demo instead of running it. I am stopping dispatches here. Nothing is in flight.

㊟ (what the first screen already tells us, which the loop did not) Reading it as you would: the "Lean concept-blending" question and "needs you: three things" are nine hours and a day old and still listed, as they should be. But "Shall I build topo4?" and "shall I draft it as a mission-style spec" were both answered, by you and by me, and are still there. The join is now good enough; the linking is what makes the brief lie. A brief that lists answered questions as awaiting you is worse than no brief, because it trains the reader to skim it.

㊭ (order, nothing dispatched until you say) 1. You run the brief in a fresh REPL and tell me in one line whether it felt like continuing a conversation or like being handed a backlog. That answer decides more than anything I can build. 2. If the backlog feeling wins, the one change worth making is to the brief's own linking: when your next operator turn in the same session says yes, ok, or go, treat the agent's last ask as answered in the brief, which is the sole-port rule applied from your side and is classical. 3. Measurement only after a week of real resumes, from the recorded briefs, not from a metric chosen now.

previous_reply_acts.text:
("ok to your 2 packets") Writing both now. On measurement, agreed, and I will put the groundwork for it into the brief packet rather than a metric I would be inventing: the brief must be recorded as a thing shown, with its item ids, so what happened to each item afterwards can be read later. Checking the two code sites first.㊢ ("ok to your 2 packets") Both running, both parked (5258efb5).
- **Mission id on every record**, codex-70, park `park-9fb7c2ee`: the seat's roster mission stamped at write time, absent when the seat has none, bells and system records included. That is the warp thread; a backfill over existing records follows once a fresh one shows the field.
- **Resume brief**, codex-71, park `park-c144f074`: classical, over one mission's records across sessions, in eight sections (seed anchors verbatim, owed to you, your asks with no answer linked, in force, adopted not applied, obligations, recently closed with the witness, facts as a typed "not read"), plus an Emacs command that inserts it at point in a REPL buffer.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("nagging to close them is not necessarily good form") Agreed, and two things in the brief packet follow from it. Your asks without a witness are headed "no answer linked", never "open", so an answered-but-unlinked ask does not read as a demand. And the brief presents state, not a to-do list: ages in days, no imperatives, closed items shown with why they closed. Most ports will not close in a session; the brief should make that look normal.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: ("we don't have a way to measure what works") True, and re-asks is a demo check, not the measure; counting closes would reward exactly the nagging you do not want. What I have put in now is only the groundwork: every brief shown is recorded with its item ids, so later turns can be joined to what was in front of the agent. No metric is computed. Candidates to weigh with you once a few briefs exist, each readable without a model: whether later turns cite brief items in their brackets; whether your turns stop restating context, which the move grammar can see as `clarify/context` or `explain/background`; and what happens to each shown item over the following week, acted on, withdrawn, or still sitting. Recorded in the mission as open, with your words.
